title: Numbers 12: Speaking Against the Man of God
body:
Read the chapter → [Numbers 12](/bible/numbers/12)

**[Numbers 12:1-2](/bible/numbers/12#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/numbers/12#v1)</sup> And Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married: for he had married an Ethiopian woman.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/numbers/12#v2)</sup> And they said, Hath the Lord indeed spoken only by Moses? hath he not spoken also by us? And the Lord heard it.

- Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married. This is still Zipporah, the daughter of the priest of Midian, whom Moses married in the forty years he dwelt outside Egypt, and whom the Lord allowed him to marry; a place being called Midian and the woman called an Ethiopian is no contradiction.
- They did not speak against Moses when he was saving them out of Egypt, nor when he set Aaron over the men and Miriam over the women; the murmuring came from somewhere else and they took hold of it. They said, Hath the LORD indeed spoken only by Moses? hath he not spoken also by us? And the LORD heard it.

  Precepts:
  - **[Exodus 2:16](/bible/exodus/2#v16)**
    > <sup>[16](/bible/exodus/2#v16)</sup> Now the priest of Midian had seven daughters: and they came and drew water, and filled the troughs to water their father’s flock.

    The priest of Midian had seven daughters who came to water their father's flock.
  - **[Exodus 2:21](/bible/exodus/2#v21)**
    > <sup>[21](/bible/exodus/2#v21)</sup> And Moses was content to dwell with the man: and he gave Moses Zipporah his daughter.

    Moses was content to dwell with the man, and he gave Moses Zipporah his daughter; this is the same woman called the Ethiopian.

**[Numbers 12:3-8](/bible/numbers/12#v3)**

> <sup>[3](/bible/numbers/12#v3)</sup> (Now the man Moses was very meek, above all the men which were upon the face of the earth.)
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/numbers/12#v4)</sup> And the Lord spake suddenly unto Moses, and unto Aaron, and unto Miriam, Come out ye three unto the tabernacle of the congregation. And they three came out.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/numbers/12#v5)</sup> And the Lord came down in the pillar of the cloud, and stood in the door of the tabernacle, and called Aaron and Miriam: and they both came forth.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/numbers/12#v6)</sup> And he said, Hear now my words: If there be a prophet among you, I the Lord will make myself known unto him in a vision, and will speak unto him in a dream.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/numbers/12#v7)</sup> My servant Moses is not so, who is faithful in all mine house.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/numbers/12#v8)</sup> With him will I speak mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches; and the similitude of the Lord shall he behold: wherefore then were ye not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?

- The man Moses was very meek, above all the men which were upon the face of the earth. The Lord suddenly called Moses, Aaron, and Miriam to the tabernacle, came down in the pillar of the cloud, and called Aaron and Miriam forth.
- He declared the difference: to a prophet He makes Himself known in a vision and speaks in a dream, but with His servant Moses, faithful in all His house, He speaks mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches. Wherefore then were ye not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?

  Precepts:
  - **[2 Peter 2:10](/bible/2-peter/2#v10)**
    > <sup>[10](/bible/2-peter/2#v10)</sup> But chiefly them that walk after the flesh in the lust of uncleanness, and despise government. Presumptuous are they, selfwilled, they are not afraid to speak evil of dignities.

    They that despise government, presumptuous and selfwilled, are not afraid to speak evil of dignities, the same spirit that speaks against the men the Most High sets up.

**[Numbers 12:9-16](/bible/numbers/12#v9)**

> <sup>[9](/bible/numbers/12#v9)</sup> And the anger of the Lord was kindled against them; and he departed.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/numbers/12#v10)</sup> And the cloud departed from off the tabernacle; and, behold, Miriam became leprous, white as snow: and Aaron looked upon Miriam, and, behold, she was leprous.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/numbers/12#v11)</sup> And Aaron said unto Moses, Alas, my lord, I beseech thee, lay not the sin upon us, wherein we have done foolishly, and wherein we have sinned.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/numbers/12#v12)</sup> Let her not be as one dead, of whom the flesh is half consumed when he cometh out of his mother’s womb.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/numbers/12#v13)</sup> And Moses cried unto the Lord, saying, Heal her now, O God, I beseech thee.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/numbers/12#v14)</sup> And the Lord said unto Moses, If her father had but spit in her face, should she not be ashamed seven days? let her be shut out from the camp seven days, and after that let her be received in again.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/numbers/12#v15)</sup> And Miriam was shut out from the camp seven days: and the people journeyed not till Miriam was brought in again.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/numbers/12#v16)</sup> And afterward the people removed from Hazeroth, and pitched in the wilderness of Paran.

- The anger of the Lord was kindled, and the cloud departed from off the tabernacle, and Miriam became leprous, white as snow. Aaron pleaded, Lay not the sin upon us; and Moses cried unto the Lord, Heal her now, O God, I beseech thee.
- The Lord answered that if her father had but spit in her face, she should be ashamed seven days; so she was shut out from the camp seven days, and the people journeyed not till Miriam was brought in again. The spit is correction, a father putting his child in her place; had she been raised to respect the men of the Lord, this would not have befallen her.
- This is a charge to raise children in the fear of the Lord and to teach them to respect the elders and the men of the Lord. Parents who let their children speak evil to the men of the Lord provoke them to wrath and bring judgment on the household.

  Precepts:
  - **[Ephesians 6:1-4](/bible/ephesians/6#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/ephesians/6#v1)</sup> Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right.
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/ephesians/6#v2)</sup> Honour thy father and mother; (which is the first commandment with promise;)
    >
    > <sup>[3](/bible/ephesians/6#v3)</sup> That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth.
    >
    > <sup>[4](/bible/ephesians/6#v4)</sup> And, ye fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.

    Children, obey your parents in the Lord; and fathers, provoke not your children to wrath, but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.
